messages:
maya_csm: Hey team — customer (AcmeFin) just flagged unusual traffic on one of their live API keys around 21:14 UTC. They think it might be an exfil attempt. They asked to rotate immediately and want confirmation on whether any PII or request payloads were stored. Can we triage?

mike_support: Copy. Can you drop the affected key id and a few sample request IDs / timestamps? I'll prep a short-term mitigation (revoke + scoped replacement) and pull logs. :lock:

maya_csm: Key id: sk_live_9f3b4a. Sample request ids: r-20260315-211402, r-20260315-211428. Customer reports source IPs they don't recognize: 54.23.12.5, 18.196.45.77.

mike_support: Doing immediate mitigation: recommend we (1) revoke the key, (2) create a new scoped key with IP allowlist for the customer, (3) rotate any downstream creds that key might have access to. I'll run revoke now and post steps so customer can rotate.

mike_support: Revoke command (running now):
```
adminctl keys revoke --id sk_live_9f3b4a --reason "suspected compromise"
```

mike_support: Creating replacement key with restricted scope & IP allowlist:
```
adminctl keys create --customer acmefin --scope generate,embeddings --ip-allowlist 52.34.1.0/24,18.196.45.0/24 --expires 30d
```

logs-bot: Retrieved logs for key sk_live_9f3b4a (partial):
```
[2026-03-15T21:14:02Z] r-20260315-211402 POST /v1/generate 200 sk_live_9f3b4a client_ip=54.23.12.5 tokens_in=42 tokens_out=128
[2026-03-15T21:14:28Z] r-20260315-211428 POST /v1/embed 200 sk_live_9f3b4a client_ip=18.196.45.77 tokens_in=12 tokens_out=512
```

logs-bot: Full payloads are archived in the audit store; I can hand off a link to the secure view once security approves.

raj_security: Thanks. A few asks: (a) preserve the logs (do not delete), (b) note IPs and correlate with other accounts, (c) check whether that key had any admin scopes or private connection roles. From the log snippet it looks like standard generate/embed calls but we need to confirm the prompt bodies.

raj_security: On retention: for hosted accounts we retain request/response bodies for 90 days in the live audit store and move to archive after that. Audit metadata (ids, timestamps, client_ip, key_id) is kept for 365 days. If this customer is on a longer retention plan, that changes.

maya_csm: Customer asking: did any of the requests return sensitive data from other customers (cross-tenant leakage)? Also asking whether we used a KMS-wrapped key for their encryption of stored objects.

raj_security: No signs of cross-tenant responses in those two request ids. We'll need to run a quick content-similarity diff across responses during the window (21:00–21:30 UTC). I'll queue that. Regarding KMS: logs show their private artifacts were encrypted using our tenant key (rkms://tenant/acmefin/primary). Is that customer-managed? I see a flag: kms_mode=redwood_managed. If they want HSM-backed CMKs we can advise a migration path.

mike_support: FYI I issued the revoke and created a temporary scoped key with an expiry. Customer notified and rotated on their side. I also set a rate throttle on the new key.

mike_support: Customer wanted a one-click playbook to rotate — shared steps:
1) Create new key in Console or via CLI.
2) Update apps to use new key (suggest feature-flag rollout).
3) Revoke old key after verifying no reconnects.

mike_support: Example CLI snippet I gave customer:
```
# create
redwood keys create --customer acmefin --label "rotated-2026-03-15" --scopes generate,embeddings
# verify
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <NEW_KEY>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/health
# revoke
redwood keys revoke --id sk_live_9f3b4a
```

maya_csm: They also asked about audit export for legal — they need a signed export showing all activity for the key between 21:00–22:00 UTC. Can we provide chain-of-custody and hash-signed logs?

raj_security: Yes, legal-grade exports are provided via the audit pipeline. I'll open an evidence bundle request. It includes time-stamped logs + SHA256 hashes + our verification signature. Expect ~2 hours for prep. I'll cc Legal once bundle is ready.

audits-bot: Audit bundle request created: bundle-20260315-acmefin-9f3b4a. ETA ~120m. Access will be via secured presigned link (MFA + access logging).

mike_support: One more mitigation suggestion to the customer: rotate any downstream secrets that may have been injected (webhooks, SSO tokens). Also advise IP allowlist and short expiry windows while investigating.

maya_csm: Customer also curious if we store prompt bodies indefinitely for private deployments (they're evaluating Private).

raj_security: For Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS/HSM and on-prem storage, data retention is controlled by their config. By default our Private package leaves logs in customer-controlled storage and does not ship request bodies to Redwood-hosted audit stores. That's part of the Private onboarding checklist.

mike_support: I'll follow up with a short FAQ for the customer: quick steps, what we store, retention windows, how to request legal-grade audit export, and the Private options.

maya_csm: Thanks all — customer is relieved but wants confirmation later that nothing sensitive was leaked. Please update thread when the similarity diff and evidence bundle are ready.

raj_security: Will do. I started the diff job (job id diff-20260315-001). I'll post results here. :eyes:
